records.title: Replication data for Towards the implementation of a more economical catalyst for hydrogen production in microbial electrolysis cells
records.publisher: CORA.Repositori de Dades de Recerca (CSUC Dataverse)
records.application_context: Experimental catalyst/electrode characterization in acetate mineral medium; not wastewater treatment evidence.
review_notes: Readme describes a 35 mL MEC with graphite-brush anode, carbon-felt or carbon-cloth cathodes, nitrogen purge, sodium acetate at 1.5 g/L, initial pH 7.5, conductivity 13 mS/cm, ambient temperature and pressure, and a 10 ohm external monitoring resistor.
Files include current-density time series, EIS and LSV; source locators are Dataverse file IDs and worksheet/cell references still need analyst extraction.
The data do not report wastewater COD, captured hydrogen yield, full hydrogen gas balance, or biosensor response/LOD/LOQ. Those absences are explicit and must not be imputed.
The linked publication is DOI 10.12688/openreseurope.22256.1; link is retained for source reconciliation, not treated as a separate reviewed record.

A first-pass file audit verified all four locally registered SHA-256 digests. The current-density sheet has 3,673 finite time coordinates over 0–25.5 days; one of six traces lacks 504 values. LSV README-vs-sheet shape and EIS formula conversion findings are preserved in artifact_review and remain unresolved for analyst review.

missing_data_reasons.wastewater_quality: Not applicable to this acetate/mineral-medium catalyst experiment; no COD/BOD/TSS record is present.
missing_data_reasons.hydrogen_output: The deposited files describe current/EIS/LSV but do not provide a reconciled gross-versus-captured H2 gas balance.
missing_data_reasons.biosensor: No biosensor calibration, analytical range, LOD/LOQ, selectivity, drift, or matrix-recovery data are included.
missing_data_reasons.quality_assurance: The source README states that no quality-assurance procedures were applicable; independent calibration/validation is not documented there.

artifact_review.method: Original ODS files were preserved. LibreOffice was used for a temporary inspection conversion. Statistics below use only rows with a finite time coordinate; no padded rows were treated as observations. No transformed workbook was added to the repository.

current_density_time_series.interpretation: Per-trace descriptive summaries only. These repeated observations are not independent replicates and must not be used to rank catalysts or validate the wastewater solver.

lsv_file.temporary_conversion_exposed: 3002 worksheet rows including header, one shared potential column and six current traces
lsv_file.review_finding: README dimensional metadata and converted column layout do not agree; preserve original and reconcile the native sheet before extracting curves. No electrode-area normalization or wastewater conditions are registered.

eis_file.review_finding: Temporary LibreOffice conversion returned #NAME? in eight secondary impedance columns. This is a conversion/formula interoperability issue to resolve against the original ODS before numeric use; no EIS fit parameters were extracted.

cross_file_limitations: The README repeats some cloth-series descriptions under the wrong catalyst names; the worksheet headers were retained as displayed and the text discrepancy remains for human review.
The experiment uses acetate mineral medium in a small MEC catalyst study, not wastewater treatment.
No reconciled gross/captured hydrogen gas measurement, gas recovery, COD/BOD/TSS dataset or independent replicate dataset is present.
Negative signed current-density values were preserved; no polarity correction or imputation was applied.

The paper reports aggregate study performance, not a sample-level holdout set. Its living air-cathode MFC charge/voltage assay is not the current static amperometric biosensor model.

records.title: On Site Evaluation of a Tubular Microbial Fuel Cell Using an Anion Exchange Membrane for Sewage Water Treatment
records.application_context: On-site tubular MFC treatment of sewage with a central air chamber and anion-exchange separator. This is a strong real-wastewater configuration candidate; the model's current oxygen boundary does not resolve the tubular geometry or depth-dependent leakage.
review_notes: Publisher abstract reports 1.3–5.7 Wh m^-3 MFC electricity production across two modules and reduced bottom-module output associated with water leakage into the air cathode.

The chemostat treatment comparison reports COD removal, BOD removal, volumetric current recovery, coulombic efficiency, external resistance, and HRT; these are literature-reported aggregated results, not independent METREV validation rows.

The article's data availability statement says raw data are available from the authors upon request. A linked CC BY 4.0 Figshare supplementary data sheet is registered separately but is not locally archived in this snapshot.

Table 1/2 display COD 450→210 mg/L for R3H12 and 450→370 mg/L for R27H12. Recomputed removals are 53.33% and 17.78%, respectively. At R27H12, 0.19 kWh/kg-COD × 0.08 kg-COD/m³ gives 0.0152 kWh/m³, whereas Table 2 displays 0.01; the difference remains an open reconciliation item. R3H12 gives 0.002064 versus displayed 0.002 kWh/m³. The paper identifies bottom-cell air-cathode water leakage and aeration energy as material loss/energy pathways, neither represented as full spatial physical losses by METREV.

records.title: Resilience of anodic biofilm in microbial fuel cell biosensor for BOD monitoring of urban wastewater
records.application_context: MFC-biofilm BOD sensor studied with synthetic and real urban wastewater and biological replicates. It is a dynamic microbial sensing method, not the current static amperometric electrode-receptor sensor model.
records.reported_raw_data_access: Authors state that datasets are available on request; no raw measurement files were locally retrieved.
review_notes: Publisher full text and supplementary PDF are open under CC BY 4.0. Results report three MFC replicates for the calibration comparison and provide method-specific aggregate performance metrics.
Results report RWW BOD dynamic range, LOD, sensitivity, response time, and signal changes during biofilm adaptation. These are candidate literature values only.
The biological MFC sensor, BOD endpoint, batch response peak and substrate-dependent biofilm behavior do not parameterize the current static electrochemical biosensor model directly.

The article explicitly reports 170 mg BOD/L as the RWW linear dynamic range, but 177 ± 7 mg BOD/L as the maximum measured undiluted RWW feed; it separately reports a 170 ± 6 mA/m² current density. These three quantities are not interchangeable. Its sensitivity equation confirms area normalization. Figure 1 current outputs are mean ± SEM over three MFC replicates and BOD concentrations are mean ± SD; Figure 2 polarization summaries are mean ± SEM over two MFCs. The main text does not define the ± statistic for every sensitivity/LOD/response aggregate, so those were left unspecified. RWW/SWW ratios and the SWW adaptation discrepancy are recorded in review_calculations. Raw data/code remain available from authors on request.
